The learning loop

EXPERIMENTAL

Adaptive blend: TimesFM, no-change, and bias-corrected TimesFM. Better performers gain relative weight; large mistakes lose weight. TimesFM’s pretrained weights stay frozen.

Score: 100 / (1 + z²), where z is the return error divided by prior 20-session volatility (minimum 0.5%). A perfect prediction scores 100; a one-volatility miss scores 50. This is a quality index, not a probability or “percent correct.”

Reward: baseline squared error − forecast squared error, both volatility-normalized. Positive beats no-change; negative earns a penalty. Direction accuracy is reported separately.

01 / THE QUESTION

One trading session ahead.

Given the information available after today’s market close, estimate the next trading session’s closing price.

The job uses the US exchange calendar, excludes unfinished sessions, and waits an hour after close. Inputs use Yahoo closing prices; recent split targets are rejected for review.

02 / THE MODEL

TimesFM, with a benchmark.

TimesFM 2.5 runs locally in a separate Python job. Every forecast will be compared with a simple no-change baseline: tomorrow’s close equals today’s.

The model uses 256 completed closing prices to predict one session ahead. Shading shows its 10th–90th quantiles; coverage is not calibrated or guaranteed.

03 / THE MEASUREMENT

Results you can inspect.

Absolute return error = |predicted close − actual close| ÷ previous close × 100, measured in percentage points.

Direction accuracy compares the signs of predicted and actual changes. Scores are calculated from actual model outputs and observed closes. The evaluation selector separates retrospective tests from prospective results.

04 / THE RECORD

Publish. Preserve. Evaluate.

Saved forecasts retain their generation time, target session, checkpoint revision, and input snapshot hash. Reruns do not overwrite predictions; they score pending outcomes.

The Tomorrow section includes an experimental adaptive blend. It learns only from scored prospective records, and is compared against the unchanged raw TimesFM forecast. Improvement is not guaranteed.

Historical tests use data downloaded today and may contain provider revisions or pretraining overlap. They are not point-in-time backtests or evidence of trading profitability. Yahoo data is used for local personal research.
